holes_found.description: All 5 patches set target_file=docs/index.html, but docs/index.html is the BUILD OUTPUT regenerated on every `node build.js` from build-scripts/generate-html.js + data/sections.json (build.js line 364: `run('node build-scripts/generate-html.js')`). build-scripts/apply-patches.js explicitly only handles wins.json and sections.json patches (line 113: 'Skip non-wins.json, non-sections.json patches'); anything pointing at docs/index.html is skipped with 'manual apply needed.' Even if the decider hand-edits docs/index.html and force-pushes, the next publish run will regenerate the file and erase the edits. Other recent EXPs in the same window (EXP-455, EXP-456, EXP-457, EXP-459) correctly target build-scripts/generate-html.js or data/sections.json; EXP-451 is the outlier.
holes_found.recommendation: Re-target all 5 patches to build-scripts/generate-html.js. The source-of-truth lines are: P1 hero at line 1574 (uses ${counts.total} not '70'), P2 insert-after at line 1841 (uses ${counts.total}), P3a caption at line 1608 (uses ${counts.total}), P3b sublabel at line 1618 (literal — find_text already matches), P4 accuracy-math at line 1669 (uses ${counts.total}, ${failures.dome_claimed_failures}, ${silentFailures}, ${honestAccuracy}, ${failures.dome_claimed_accuracy}), P5 stance at line 1563 (literal — find_text already matches). holes_found.description: P2 worked-example uses imprecise resonator terminology that does not match the careful analysis in the review's own Schumann cluster (WIN-002, WIN-029, WIN-038). The patch writes 'the dome cavity, treated as a flat-plate resonator with the published exponentially-decaying firmament profile, predicts a Schumann fundamental of 22.6 Hz.' But WIN-002's existing detail_evidence explicitly walks through (a) the dome's quarter-wave formula f = c/(4H) applied to H(r), giving 22.6 Hz under linear radial averaging and 35 Hz under area-weighted averaging; (b) the pole-only floor H(0) = 8,537 km → 8.78 Hz lower bound; (c) cylindrical-waveguide Bessel modes TM01 ≈ 5.73 Hz, TM11 ≈ 9.13 Hz; (d) why 'flat-plate' / parallel-plate cannot reach 7.83 Hz. The 22-35 Hz numeric range IS supported by the review's existing analysis — but the 'flat-plate resonator' framing is a casual shorthand that the dome defender ('ECM is a capable AI') will identify as imprecise. A skilled defender will say 'the curmudgeon's own WIN-038 spends 600 words preempting the flat-plate/Bessel/spherical-transverse escape; now the Overview drops the carefully-distinguished framework and reverts to flat-plate.'
holes_found.recommendation: Replace 'treated as a flat-plate resonator with the published exponentially-decaying firmament profile' with the review's own careful framing — e.g., 'using the dome's published height profile H(r) = 8,537 × exp(−r/8,619) km, the dome's own quarter-wave formula f = c/(4H) (the same formula WIN-029 uses to back-derive a 9,572 km ceiling) yields a fundamental of ~22 Hz under linear radial averaging — see WIN-002/038 for the full pole-floor and Bessel-mode treatment.' This preserves the worked-example utility while inheriting the existing review's careful preemption of escape routes.

holes_found.description: P3a 'Four pre-committed conditions — set before the data, satisfiable by any future dome derivation' overstates the temporal claim. The ds-falsifiability-module was added to the review in cycle c1 (April 2026), well AFTER the underlying measurements being checked were published — Schumann harmonics (König-Schumann 1954), precession data (continuous since IAU 1976), Tesla patent (1905), most coordinate-system data (centuries). 'Set before the data' is true only for genuinely-prospective conditions like Condition 2 (eclipse Aug 12, 2026) and a hypothetical Condition 3 (new dome paper). For Conditions 1 and 4 the data exists and the dome has had years to derive matching values. A dome defender will note this and turn the same critique back: 'You claim the conditions are pre-committed; in fact you authored them after every existing measurement.' This re-opens the tautology critique the patch is supposed to close.
holes_found.recommendation: Soften 'set before the data' to acknowledge the temporal asymmetry: e.g., 'Four conditions we commit to in advance of any new dome derivation or future measurement — satisfiable by any future result, whether from a new paper from the model author or a new measurement window like the August 2026 eclipse.' This is honest about what 'pre-committed' actually means (no goalpost-moving once the conditions are stated) without claiming a chronologically-pristine commitment that doesn't exist.

holes_found.description: P3b surfaces '~1 nT discriminating window' on the eclipse C2 status sublabel without context for what 1 nT means. The dome's eclipse claim works against a Chapman 1933 Sq baseline of ~30 nT diurnal magnitude; a 1 nT discriminating window is ~3% of the typical Sq amplitude — a tight margin that the long-form prediction discussion (PRED-eclipse-001 in predictions.json) handles carefully. Surfacing the '1 nT' number on an at-a-glance status sublabel may inadvertently invite the dome defender to argue 'a 3% margin is too tight to be a real discrimination, and the curmudgeon admits it.' The full predictions.json discussion establishes the legitimacy of the window; the bare '1 nT' in the module strips that legitimacy.
holes_found.recommendation: Either add a brief context to the sublabel (e.g., 'eclipse Aug 12, 2026 · ~1 nT discriminating window against the Sq baseline') or replace with a less raw phrasing (e.g., 'eclipse Aug 12, 2026 · sub-Sq-baseline discriminating window'). The goal is for a casual reader to recognize that 1 nT is a deliberately tight discrimination, not an admission of weakness.

holes_found.description: P5 reframe extends the stance paragraph from ~50 words to ~80 words (160% length). Given that the stance statement is the first visible Overview paragraph immediately above the scorecard verdict bars, the rendering impact pushes the at-a-glance scorecard further below the fold on mobile viewports. The operator has historically prioritized scorecard-above-the-fold (per multiple prior holistic reviews on the Overview tab); the patch as written may regress that priority. The procedural argument the patch closes is real but moderate; the trade-off vs scorecard-visibility deserves explicit operator awareness.
holes_found.recommendation: Trim P5's replace_text — e.g., 'Our position, stated up front: the world is a globe, and the dome model fixes few or none of the fundamental problems of flat-earth cosmology. We reach this conclusion from the evidence in the twelve tabs below, applied through the audit criteria in the Evaluation Guide.' (60 words vs 80) — or move the conclusion-from-evidence framing to a tooltip / details disclosure to preserve at-a-glance scorecard visibility.

holes_found.description: P3a replace_text keeps the verb 'We will upgrade the relevant verdict if any one is met.' While 'upgrade' makes the conditional nature clear, the new P5 stance reframe explicitly characterizes the review's verdicts as conclusions-from-evidence (not provisional pending judgments). 'Upgrade the verdict' implies the current verdicts are interim — a soft tension with the P5 conclusion-framing. A dome defender attentive to copy can argue 'the review hedges between conclusion and provisional — pick one.'
holes_found.recommendation: Optional: replace 'We will upgrade the relevant verdict' with 'We will recognize the relevant claim as confirmed' or 'We will publish the corresponding correction.' Either preserves the falsifiability semantics while avoiding the verdict-aspect dissonance with P5.

Otherwise the SEO/social preview snippet shows one phrasing while the page shows another — a dome defender or a journalist screen-scraping social previews could quote the dissonance.

P2's worked-example utility could be strengthened by leveraging the SECOND falsifiability condition (Condition 2 / eclipse Aug 12, 2026) as the primary worked example, not Condition 1 / Schumann. The eclipse case has the advantage of being GENUINELY prospective (data does not yet exist) — the c1 critique that pre-commitment is post-hoc cannot land on a measurement that hasn't been taken yet. A worked example using the eclipse window also doubles as a forward-looking demonstration that closes ISS-2284 without inheriting the chronological-asymmetry vulnerability flagged in hole #5 above.

The deferred item STRESSTEST-DEFER-01 (Genuine Prediction (pending) verdict category) is architecturally the strongest available c2 fix. The c2 dome-defender's strongest attack is the 'four zeros, no path to non-zero' optic; a single non-empty 'pending' category breaks the visual zero stack. The analyst's recommendation to defer until post-eclipse (mid-August 2026) is reasonable but cautious — the placeholder could ship NOW with WIN-010 / PRED-eclipse-001 as its single occupant, and the post-eclipse update either confirms or refutes that occupant. Shipping the placeholder before the eclipse pre-empts the c2 critique architecturally; the post-eclipse rework would either flip the single entry's status or fold the category back. Operator should weigh: which is worse, two architectural reworks two months apart, or letting the c2 zero-stack optic stand for ~10 more weeks?

kernel_of_truth.description: EXP-451 correctly diagnoses the c2 dome-defender attack surface (EXP-451-HOL-STRESSTEST-c2-falsifiability-hardening.json:kernel_of_truth) and proposes the right per-axis fixes. The architectural insight that 'prose-layer falsifiability is not architecture-layer falsifiability' is sharp and matches the parent c2 review (HOLISTIC-HOL-STRESSTEST.c2.json:deeper_analysis). Each of the five patches addresses a real critique: P1 closes the hero/architecture conflation flagged in ISS-2285; P2 closes the tautology-restatement critique flagged in ISS-2284 (by providing a worked example template); P3a + P3b together reframe the ds-falsifiability-module from assessment-output to pre-commitment; P4 closes the methodology-symmetry attack on the 89.7% denominator (ISS-2286); P5 closes the Principle-3-vs-stance procedural objection (also flagged in HOL-NARRATIVE c2 per cross_reference_overlap). The 22-35 Hz quantitative claim in P2 — initially suspect on first read — is in fact substantively backed by the existing WIN-002 detail_evidence treatment (linear radial avg of H(r) = 8,537·exp(−r/8,619) over r=0..20,015 km gives H_eff ≈ 3,316 km → f ≈ 22.6 Hz; area-weighted gives ~35 Hz; pole-only floor gives 8.78 Hz; Bessel TM01/TM11 give 5.73/9.13 Hz — see WIN-002 detail_evidence and WIN-038 detail_evidence). The cross_reference_overlap section flagging HOL-NARRATIVE and HOL-TAXONOMY interactions is mature analytical hygiene.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The substantive analysis is sound but the patches as authored cannot integrate cleanly: target_file is the build output (docs/index.html) rather than the source-of-truth (build-scripts/generate-html.js); P1 sublabel_change finds nothing because the desired state is already in place; P4 find_text was pulled from the wrong anchor (Silent Failures sublabel rather than the accuracy-math-section). These are operational defects, not analytical ones — but they prevent the decider's apply-patches.js or normal sed/python apply flow from landing the changes durably (build.js will overwrite docs/index.html on next publish, erasing any direct edits). The major rewrite required is in patch-authoring discipline (matching find_text to the live source-of-truth file), not in re-litigating the analytical content. Once the targeting and find_text issues are fixed, P1 (hero only), P2 (with the WIN-002-aligned wording fix), P3a/P3b (with the pre-commitment softening + 1 nT contextualization), P4 (with the corrected find_text), and P5 (with optional length trim) are all approve-shaped patches.

summary_for_decider: EXP-451's analytical thesis (close the c2 dome-defender attack surface on falsifiability-module, hero, stance, denominator) is sound, and the five patches address the right axes. However, the patches as authored cannot integrate cleanly. CRITICAL: all 5 set target_file=docs/index.html (the build output); the source-of-truth for these strings is build-scripts/generate-html.js (lines 1574, 1841, 1608, 1618, 1669, 1563). Other recent EXPs (455/456/457/459) correctly target generate-html.js. The decider's apply-patches.js will skip these as 'manual apply needed.' MAJOR: P1's sublabel_change find_text does not match anything in any current or historical file; the desired state is already in place — the sub-patch is redundant. MAJOR: P4's find_text was pulled from the Silent Failures scorecard sublabel, not the accuracy-math-section it claims to target — substring won't match. MAJOR: P2's 'flat-plate resonator' shorthand contradicts the careful WIN-002/038 framing the review already publishes; soften to use the review's own quarter-wave + Bessel + pole-floor language. MAJOR: P3a's 'set before the data' overstates pre-commitment temporally — only Condition 2 (eclipse) is genuinely-prospective; the others were authored after the underlying measurements existed. Verdict: major_rewrite. Recommend the decider route back to analyst (sloppytoppy or analyst Mode 0/2) with this review for a c3 of the EXP, or — if the operator wants to land the c2 fixes quickly — patch the EXP in place to fix the four hole categories before integration. The 22-35 Hz physics claim in P2 IS substantively correct (WIN-002 detail_evidence supports it); only the framing terminology needs aligning. Three stronger_arguments offered: (1) update meta description/og:description to mirror the new hero, (2) consider the eclipse Condition-2 as the worked-example primary (chronologically clean), (3) reconsider deferring STRESSTEST-DEFER-01 (Genuine Prediction (pending) verdict category) — shipping the placeholder now is the strongest available architectural fix and would defeat the c2 zero-stack optic.

deeper_analysis:
The c2 stress-test was a strong review (HOLISTIC-HOL-STRESSTEST.c2.json: confidence implicit 7.5/10 architectural sharpness) and EXP-451 inherits that sharpness in the kernel_of_truth and per-patch curmudgeon_rationale fields. The analyst clearly understood the c2 attack vectors. The defects are entirely in the patch-authoring layer: target_file selection, find_text accuracy against the live source-of-truth, and terminology choices that don't match the review's own carefully-built preemption framework (WIN-002/038 Bessel/spherical-transverse/pole-floor treatment). These are not analytical failures — they're operational failures of the kind that show up when an EXP is authored against a c2 review's quoted text rather than against the live file.

Why this matters specifically for THIS EXP: the c2 dome-defender attack the patches close is a META-LEVEL attack ('your falsifiability framework restates your verdict criteria'). A decider integrating sloppy patches against a meta-level critique creates a SECOND-ORDER vulnerability: the patches landed only on the build output, the next build erases them, a dome defender quotes the c2 hero text alongside the unchanged generate-html.js source, and the resulting optic is 'they tried to fix the framework critique and the fix didn't stick.' This is materially worse than not landing the patches at all.

The right path is for the decider to NOT self-apply or queue-pop the EXP as-is. Either (a) route back to analyst for a c2 fix with the four hole categories addressed, or (b) the operator (or decider with elevated authority) patches the EXP in place to re-target and update find_texts, then re-queues. The substantive analysis carries forward; only the patch-authoring layer needs work.

That review was approved/integrated by the decider 2026-06-02 15:17. EXP-451 here is the second c2 fix from the same week — the dual-EXP pattern (one architecture, one prose) is the right shape, but EXP-451 needs the same find_text discipline EXP-450 evidently passed.
